title: repository.publish_resolve is wired in the daemon registry and fenced to the operator: human-only, MCP-excluded
description:
ROW 3 of 4 for task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 ("An UNKNOWN publish effect has no operator exit"), filed by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18. Depends on row 2 (the refusal vocabulary, which itself follows row 1's roster slice task-f3182818). task-21be6e90 (the behaviour) depends on this row. Precedent: `preview.decide`'s task-5f883e4e and `release.decide`'s task-54b74b80.

WHAT IT WIRES. The payload keys (e.g. `[\"decisionId\", \"resolution\"]`, `resolution` being `NOT_TRANSMITTED` or `ABANDON`) in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts beside `\"repository.publish\"` (:184); the registry entry, following how release.decide is registered as an async entry in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts; and membership of OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:379. The handler this row registers may REFUSE every dispatch with a stable code until task-21be6e90 lands the behaviour — it must never pretend to resolve.

HUMAN-ONLY BY THE EXISTING DERIVATION. Resolving an UNKNOWN publish is the operator asserting that the remote does not hold a sha; only they can make that call. Adding the kind to OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS makes it human-only AND removes it from the MCP roster automatically, because `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` is DERIVED from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts). The MCP stdio entry authenticates with the operator credential as its fallback, so an operator kind advertised over MCP would be an agent arriving AS the operator; the derived exclusion is the fence, and this row must not hand-type a second exclusion list.

PINNED CONSUMERS THIS MOVES, and the rule for them. apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:278 pins `{ excluded: 29, queries: 7, vocabulary: 65, wired: 43 }` at HEAD 2026-09-18; an operator-only kind moves `vocabulary` and `excluded` and leaves `wired` unchanged. Per this epic's rail, NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT IN A DoD: run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative, because a concurrent kind-publishing row can move the same literal first. Also census apps/daemon/src/gates-human-only-fence.test.ts and apps/daemon/src/gates-roster-coherence.test.ts (which classifies every roster kind), plus any MCP-exclusion or vocabulary test the full-tree grep turns up. If the census exceeds this row's path cap, split before submitting.

OUT OF SCOPE: the resolve behaviour, the persisted observation and the Publish card (task-21be6e90).
definitionOfDone: `repository.publish_resolve` has payload keys, a registry entry and OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS membership; a dispatch by a non-operator principal is refused with the registry's operator-fence code, asserted by value WITH its layer.

The kind is absent from `wiredMcpToolKinds()` through the EXISTING derivation (no hand-typed exclusion added), proven by an arm; and the bidirectional allowlist arms in mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts pass, with the pinned counts at :278 re-aimed from the leg's PRINTED expected-vs-received rather than a number frozen in advance.
Until task-21be6e90 lands, an operator dispatch of the kind is refused with a stable, named code — never accepted, never a silent no-op — asserted by value.
gates-human-only-fence.test.ts and gates-roster-coherence.test.ts classify the new kind as human-only, and the completion record names every file the census found and its verdict.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed` lines: the full `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, and `pnpm typecheck`.

(2) apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts: add the kind to REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_FAMILY (or the family step 1 justified) with a capability chosen for a stated reason — the operator holds every capability, so it gates only REACH for other principals; add it to the wired-kind type union and to OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS; and give `familyCapabilityOf` whatever the family needs, following preview.decide. (3) apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-families.ts: its family classification, if preview.decide's pattern at :126 requires one. (4) apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts: a registry entry beside release.decide's (:353) whose handler REFUSES every dispatch with a stable, named code — prefer an existing registry code meaning 'recognised but not yet serviceable' over minting one for a stub task-a47babf8 will replace, and say so in a comment naming that row. Pin the fence and the stub by dispatch, in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts, each asserting the code AND its layer by value — never merely that the dispatch failed, because more than one layer can refuse and an arm that checks only the outcome stays green when the fence moves to a weaker layer (global rail). (DoD 1) A NON-operator principal dispatching `repository.publish_resolve` is refused by the registry's operator fence, with that fence's own code and layer. (DoD 3) The OPERATOR dispatching it is refused by the stub with the stable code step 3 chose — never accepted and never a silent no-op. planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Filed by me today as ROW 3 of the owner-directed split of task-21be6e90. dependsOn row 2 (task-adeabf1f), which follows row 1 (task-f3182818). The service child task-a47babf8 replaces this row's refusing stub with the real behaviour. Measured at HEAD 2026-09-18.

(1) THE TEMPLATE IS preview.decide, NOT repository.publish. `repository.publish` is a BOOTSTRAP kind (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts:44) with a bootstrap-sequence entry (bootstrap-sequence.ts:29, :176) — joining that family would drag the bootstrap sequence in. `preview.decide`, a non-bootstrap operator decision, is wired through: its payload keys (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:37, :167); its family map with a capability (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:169-171, `CAPABILITIES.REVIEW`); the wired-kind type union (:255); `familyCapabilityOf` (:296); OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (:401); and a family classification in daemon-command-families.ts (:126). It never touches the bootstrap sequence.

(2) THE REGISTRATION HOME. `release.decide`, the other operator decide kind, is registered in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts:353 as `[RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND]: Object.freeze({ ... payloadKeys: PAYLOAD_KEYS[...], requiredCapability: CAPABILITIES.GOAL })`. That file already holds preview.* and deployment.* operator entries; the refusing stub goes there.

(3) A SEMANTIC HOME ALREADY EXISTS. `REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_FAMILY = Object.freeze({ "repository.recover": CAPABILITIES.ADMIN })` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:181, composed at :278). Resolving a stuck publish is a repository RECOVERY action, and repository.recover is already operator-only. Joining that family keeps the kind out of the bootstrap sequence entirely. The worker confirms it adds no sequence coupling and chooses the capability with a stated reason.

(4) THE CENSUS, and how it was nearly missed. A first `git grep` of kind-count pins returned almost nothing because `git grep` does not recurse `**` without the `:(glob)` magic — it silently skipped mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts, which holds a pin known to exist. That is exactly the 'a sweep that yields zero cases passes' failure the rails warn about. Re-run with `:(glob)`, the pins a new operator-only kind moves are: apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:157 (`expect(MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(...)`, an exact list); :228-249 (`expectedExcluded`, documented as an 'EXACT, frozen exclusion denominator', listing every excluded kind by hand); and :278 (`{ excluded: 29, queries: 7, vocabulary: 65, wired: 43 }` — `excluded` and `vocabulary` each rise by one, `wired` does not). :258-259 is DERIVED from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and needs no edit. apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:465 pins `expect(OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS.size).toBe(30)`. Of the fourteen test files that reference OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, a triage found only daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts pinning the WHOLE set; the other thirteen check membership of specific kinds, which a new kind cannot disturb. That triage is a regex and is not proof: the worker's own full daemon run is the final census.

(5) gates-roster-coherence.test.ts NEEDS NO EDIT, contrary to this row's description. It checks roster COHERENCE — served is a subset of advertised (:79-85), the generated client equals the roster (:89-94), and every band kind is on all three surfaces (:97-108) — not human-only classification. With row 1 advertising the kind and this row serving it, it is satisfied as-is. Human-only classification is gates-human-only-fence.test.ts plus the derived MCP exclusion.
